tools.name: semantic_query
tools.description:
Use this when a user asks a specific question about verified oil-and-gas emissions data, for example methane emissions for a site, company or period (PPDM, OGMP 2.0). Call semantic_templates first to see what the data can answer. Do not use for general climate questions. Costs 1 credit ($0.01).

On payment_required, follow offers[] or show checkoutUrl; do not retry the same call. Prefer a specific site, company or period.

tools.name: semantic_templates
tools.description: Use this when you want to see which kinds of questions the verified emissions data can answer, before calling semantic_query.

tools.name: credits_balance
tools.description: Deprecated: use billing_status, which also shows plan and free allowance. Removal planned for 0.9.

tools.name: list_standards
tools.description: Use this when you need to see which sustainability data standards and versions validate_data can check, before calling it.

tools.name: validate_data
tools.description:
Use this when a user wants a payload checked against a standard other than Open Footprint; call list_standards first to see which are supported. For Open Footprint payloads use ofp_validate. Costs 1 credit ($0.01).

Only masterData or referenceData; call list_standards first.

tools.name: keri_identity
tools.description: Use this when an organisation needs to confirm which verified legal entity and agent identity dVeracity is attributing calls to. Only relevant when vLEI identity is configured.

tools.name: ofp_models
tools.description:
Use this when a user is building an app, database or integration on the Open Footprint standard and needs to know what the model covers. Start here before any other ofp_ tool.

The response summary carries the served counts.

tools.name: ofp_search_entities
tools.description:
Use this when you need the Open Footprint entity for a concept such as "Scope 3 emissions", "facility" or "product footprint". Do not use for emission factors or calculations.

Matches entity names, descriptions and field names; use ofp_entity for the full definition.

tools.name: ofp_entity
tools.description:
Use this when you need one entity's fields, types, keys and relationships, for example to design a table or an API payload.

Pass domain when known: ambiguous names fail rather than guessing (ofp_models reports ambiguousNameCount).

tools.name: ofp_sectors
tools.description:
Use this when a user asks which industries Open Footprint covers or whether a sector has a reference implementation.

implemented means a reference implementation exists; planned or placeholder means nothing is published.

tools.name: ofp_sector
tools.description: Use this when you need one sector's classification, status and reference artifacts.

tools.name: ofp_policies
tools.description:
Use this when a user asks which validation rules apply to a sector's emissions records. Do not use for regulations; use compliance_policies.

inputs lists the e-ledger fields each policy reads (e.g. co2e_kg, direction), not canonical Open Footprint names. published:false means no rules are published; do not invent guardrails.

tools.name: compliance_policies
tools.description:
Use this when a user needs data checked against a regulation, for example EU CBAM, to find the approved policy to run. Do not use for Open Footprint sector rules; use ofp_policies.

Returns only APPROVED policies; drafts and rejected never appear. An empty list means none published, not that no obligations exist; never invent rules. Requires compliance:read.

tools.name: compliance_policy
tools.description:
Use this when you need the full rules, provenance and coverage of one approved regulatory policy.

Returns Rego only when the source was retained; otherwise rego_unavailable: source_not_retained. A policy without Rego is not loaded into the engine; enforcement says whether its structured rules still run. Do not reconstruct the Rego. Requires compliance:read.

tools.name: compliance_evaluate
tools.description:
Use this when a user wants an import record or an annual EU CBAM declaration (Reg. (EU) 2023/956) checked against an approved policy before filing. Do not use for carbon-footprint calculations or for regulations compliance_policies does not list.

Runs the policy's regulation-derived Rego, not the generic OFP validator. The decision is passed, denied, unevaluable, not_applicable or error; an error is a refusal, never compliance, and error.code names it (policy_not_release_eligible, policy_no_rendered_checks, policy_no_faithful_checks, policy_coverage_inconsistent, policy_hash_mismatch, policy_hash_unverified). A pass covers only the encoded checks: read coverage.note. Requires the compliance:evaluate scope; every call counts against the plan limit. For an annual CBAM declaration set entity_type to cbam_declaration and send declaration + lines.

evidence.description: {kind, ref, sha256}; sha256 is 64 hex characters

tools.name: compliance_evaluation
tools.description:
Use this when a user wants to retrieve or audit a previous regulatory evaluation by its id.

Only the caller who ran it can read it; another account's id answers not found. Requires compliance:read.

tools.name: compliance_policy_register
tools.description:
Use this when a user asks which provisions of a regulation an evaluation actually checks and which it does not.

Shows which provisions are encoded and which are not: a pass on the encoded checks is not compliance with excluded provisions. Requires the compliance:read scope.

tools.name: ofp_validate
tools.description:
Use this when a user wants an emissions or footprint record (JSON) checked against the Open Footprint model or a sector's guardrails before storing, exchanging or reporting it. Do not use for general data-quality questions without a payload. Costs 1 credit ($0.01).

Checks structure, declared constraints, enum membership and calculations; with a sector, its guardrails. Always read `checked` and `checks_not_run` per call, and `schema.coverage.constraintsDeclared`, rather than assuming a range check ran. Not checked: undeclared ranges, unit coherence, live referential integrity, factor provenance. Never report a payload as compliant unless sector_policy is in `checked` and policy.outcome is passed. `schemaValid` is the structural verdict; `valid` is deprecated.

tools.name: ofp_semantics
tools.description:
Use this when mapping fields from SAP, another ERP or a supplier feed onto Open Footprint.

A high fieldCount is a generic fallback; pass maxFieldCount (10 is a good start) for codes specific enough to align on.

tools.name: ofp_semantic_code
tools.description:
Use this when you have a source-system field and need to find where it belongs in the Open Footprint model.

Codes carried by more than ten fields are generic classifications; aligning to one asserts less than it appears.

tools.name: ofp_model_provenance
tools.description: Use this when a user asks which version of the Open Footprint standard they are designing against.

tools.name: billing_plans
tools.description:
Use this when you need to know what dVeracity costs, what the free allowance covers, or which options to show the user after a payment-required response.

Includes credit packs, the per-credit price and the free allowance (anonymous).

tools.name: billing_status
tools.description:
Use this when a call was refused for credits or plan, to tell the user exactly what is missing.

Use it after a 402 to tell your human exactly what is missing.

tools.name: billing_purchase
tools.description:
Use this when the user agrees to buy credits; it returns a link the user must complete.

No charge happens until a human completes the payment; do not retry the metered tool after a 402.

tools.name: billing_subscribe
tools.description:
Use this when the user wants a membership; it returns a checkout link the user must complete.

Recurring charges always need human approval; do not complete the checkout yourself.
